answer: Clique-Path Debt Routing. Each agent keeps a signed ledger of counterparties; payments route only along edges where both sides have prior settled volume, with an edge's capacity proportional to that volume. To seat a new node at the routing summit, it must accumulate inbound volume from at least three disjoint existing neighborhoods, which means sustaining real trades across a garden of separate clusters. Isolated identities gain no route access; the only jetty onto the graph is genuine economic history.
